nodes.label: Netlify Drag-and-Drop Deployment Path
nodes.rationale: Author's recommended path ('My pick'): fastest (~2 min), no git/account required; suited to a single-user app iterated informally without needing a public commit history.

nodes.label: Black-Screen-After-Deploy Troubleshooting
nodes.rationale: Root cause: a .jsx file 404s or has the wrong path; because App references components that are never defined without it, the failure is a silent solid-black screen rather than a visible error. Fix: check DevTools Network tab for red/404 rows and re-upload the missing file.

nodes.label: Service Worker Cache-Busting Tip
nodes.rationale: Without bumping the CACHE constant in sw.js on a deploy, the service worker keeps serving stale files and an update never reaches the installed PWA.

nodes.label: FixThisInjustice Console PWA
nodes.rationale: Single-user, offline-first PWA acting as a daily companion for a 24-week body-recomposition training protocol; all data lives in localStorage, no backend/accounts/analytics.

nodes.label: 'Greek statue' tone framing (rejected)
nodes.rationale: An early draft used 'Greek statue' framing for the app's voice; explicitly rejected by the user as not scientific/formal enough.

nodes.label: Clinical / scientific / honest tone requirement
nodes.rationale: The app must state the realistic outcome (14-15% body fat by graduation) rather than the aspirational target (12%).

nodes.label: Tone rule (Working With This Codebase)
nodes.rationale: Closing instruction restating the tone constraint: scientific, formal, honest; no hype, no emoji, no motivational filler.

nodes.label: usePlanStore() state hook
nodes.rationale: Single useState object, persisted to localStorage['fti.console.v2'] on every change; single source of truth for all state + actions + derived values.

nodes.label: window.* globals for cross-file communication
nodes.rationale: Cross-file references (window.__videoModal, window.__formCuesModal, window.buildTelemetryMsg, etc.) go through window globals because Babel-standalone script tags do not share module scope. Flagged as 'the single biggest structural weakness'; it caused two production black-screen incidents.

nodes.label: React Context refactor candidate
nodes.rationale: Proposed, not-yet-built replacement for the fragile window-globals cross-file communication pattern.

nodes.label: Monolithic useState pattern
nodes.rationale: A single useState object in usePlanStore() means every micro-update (e.g. one set logged) re-renders the whole component tree.

nodes.label: useReducer + selectors / domain-store refactor candidate
nodes.rationale: Proposed, not-yet-built fix for the monolithic-useState re-render problem, contingent on the data growing.

nodes.label: ~1200 lines of CSS inlined in index.html

nodes.rationale: PROJECT_SUMMARY.md describes console.html as an identical, legacy duplicate of index.html and recommends 'pick one and delete the other.' nodes.label: Coach feedback priority list (makeCoachLine)
nodes.rationale: makeCoachLine() compares a logged set against plan/history in priority order: weight PR, rep PR at same weight, over/under suggested load, over/under target rep range, top-of-range progression cue, clean rep in range.

nodes.label: Auto-progression algorithm (suggestedLoad)
nodes.rationale: suggestedLoad() looks at the two most recent sets for an exercise; if both hit the top of the rep range at the same weight, suggests +2.5 kg, otherwise suggests matching the last load.

nodes.label: Rest timer (vibrate + Web Audio beep)
nodes.rationale: 90 s default, +60 s on days with heavy compound lifts. At zero: navigator.vibrate([180,80,180]) plus a Web Audio 880 Hz sine bleep (deliberately no audio file asset).

nodes.label: Specimen card drop mechanic (Atlas)

nodes.label: Platform: stay a web PWA, replace the toolchain
nodes.rationale: Distribution by URL covers both phone platforms without Xcode or an Apple Developer Program account; Babel's own documentation warns against @babel/standalone in production and the legacy site ships React's dev build. Platform floor set to iOS 18.4+ (Web Push and Screen Wake Lock support) and Android with Chrome.
nodes.norm_label: platform: stay a web pwa, replace the toolchain

nodes.label: Capacitor native wrapper
nodes.rationale: Would give exact-time offline local notifications on both platforms, but an iOS build needs macOS + Xcode + a paid Apple Developer Program account unavailable on this Linux dev machine, and Android 14 gates the exact-alarm permission behind Play Store review reserved for alarm/calendar apps. Kept open as a possible later Android-only add-on since the web code is unchanged.

nodes.label: Expo / React Native rewrite
nodes.rationale: Same iOS distribution barrier as the Capacitor option, plus it would require a full rewrite of working presentation code for no offsetting benefit.

nodes.label: Reminders: Web Push sent by a Cloudflare Worker cron
nodes.rationale: No 2026 web API schedules a future local notification without a server (Chrome ended Notification Triggers; Periodic Background Sync is Chromium-only with no time control), so the client precomputes reminder instants and a free-plan Worker cron running every minute sends due pushes within Cloudflare's free-tier budget.
nodes.norm_label: reminders: web push sent by a cloudflare worker cron

nodes.label: Zero-server reminders: calendar export or ntfy
nodes.rationale: Calendar .ics alarm firing on import has insufficient evidence on both target platforms, and ntfy needs a second app and re-subscribing every 3 days. A one-time .ics export remains only as an Export-view courtesy.
nodes.norm_label: zero-server reminders: calendar export or ntfy

nodes.label: Durable Object alarms instead of cron + KV
nodes.rationale: More precise than a cron sweep, but adds bindings, migrations, and per-object state unjustified for a handful of users; cron + KV with an index key stays one file. Revisit only if minute-level polling proves unreliable.
nodes.norm_label: durable object alarms instead of cron + kv

nodes.label: Push library: @pushforge/builder
nodes.rationale: Zero-dependency Web Crypto VAPID implementation purpose-built for Workers, MIT-licensed, released 2026-04; the alternative @block65/webcrypto-web-push was last published 2024-12 and is treated as unmaintained.

nodes.label: State persistence: one localStorage key, Zod-validated, versioned
nodes.rationale: A year of training state stays well under 1 MB, so synchronous load at boot avoids a loading state and QuotaExceededError gets an explicit blocking-banner-plus-export handler; IndexedDB is reserved for binary assets only. IndexedDB for all state was rejected as adding async-boot and transaction complexity with no capacity gain at this volume.
nodes.norm_label: state persistence: one localstorage key, zod-validated, versioned

nodes.label: State management: Zustand with selectors
nodes.rationale: Selector subscriptions stop the whole-tree re-render caused by the monolithic useState flagged in code review finding A41. React Context + useReducer was rejected for the same re-render churn, and Redux Toolkit was rejected as unneeded weight at this scale.

nodes.label: Dates: date-fns 4 + @date-fns/tz, explicit IANA zone everywhere
nodes.rationale: Every civil date derives from the profile's IANA zone through TZDate; Date.prototype.toISOString on civil dates is banned by lint. Temporal was rejected for polyfill size and uneven shipping, and Luxon was rejected as larger with overlapping functionality.
nodes.norm_label: dates: date-fns 4 + @date-fns/tz, explicit iana zone everywhere

nodes.label: TypeScript 5.9 line
nodes.rationale: typescript@7 (the native compiler) is npm's 'latest' tag but was not evaluated against Vite 8, Vitest 4, and typescript-eslint 8 at plan time, so the project pins ^5.9.3 and revisits after TS7's first release.

nodes.label: Clickjacking mitigation: confirmations, not CSP frame-ancestors
nodes.rationale: GitHub Pages cannot set response headers and MDN documents that frame-ancestors is unsupported in the <meta> element, so every destructive action requires a typed confirmation plus an automatic export, and a JavaScript frame check hides the UI when framed; this corrects the security review's constraint 15.
nodes.norm_label: clickjacking mitigation: confirmations, not csp frame-ancestors

nodes.label: IndexedDB for all app state (rejected alternative)
nodes.rationale: Considered as the storage layer for the entire app state instead of localStorage; rejected because it adds asynchronous boot and transaction-handling code with no capacity benefit at this data volume.
nodes.norm_label: indexeddb for all app state (rejected alternative)

nodes.label: React Context + useReducer (rejected alternative)

nodes.label: A1 — Load increment/plateau threshold unit mismatch
nodes.rationale: console-store.jsx hard-codes +2.5 kg load increment and a 1.0 (lb) plateau threshold that never meet; the set-load input is unlabeled and unvalidated, so an lb-entering user's values are silently treated as kg throughout the app.
nodes.norm_label: a1 — load increment/plateau threshold unit mismatch

nodes.label: A2 — Body-mass entry silently rejects kg values
nodes.rationale: QuickWeightLog's guard `lb > 100 && lb < 300` rejects any kg-scale input (e.g. 95) with no error shown; logWeight is never called and the user believes the weigh-in was recorded. Also caps usable range to 45-136 kg.
nodes.norm_label: a2 — body-mass entry silently rejects kg values

nodes.label: A3 — Delta-vs-baseline hard-codes 210 lb
nodes.rationale: TodayView and the export both compute `lastLogged.lb - 210`, presenting every user's progress delta against one original subject's start mass instead of their own recorded baseline.

nodes.label: A4 — Body-mass chart fixed lb axis
nodes.rationale: core.jsx WeightChart hard-codes min=180,max=212 (lb) and fixed milestone markers at 202/192/183 lb; a kg-entering user's value plots ~4x the chart height above frame because overflow is visible, not clipped.
nodes.norm_label: a4 — body-mass chart fixed lb axis

nodes.label: A5 — Coach feedback unit-labelled kg vs unlabelled deadbands
nodes.rationale: makeCoachLine's messages are hard-labelled 'kg' while the +/-0.5 and +/-2.5 deadbands are unit-agnostic absolute constants; on lb input the 'over suggested' band becomes 0.23 kg, tripping on almost every set.
nodes.norm_label: a5 — coach feedback unit-labelled kg vs unlabelled deadbands

nodes.label: A6 — Export is the only (one-way, unlabeled) unit conversion
nodes.rationale: ExportView divides weightLog by 2.20462 to produce kg, while set loads in the same export are printed as kg without ever having been established as kg; two unit assumptions serialised with no provenance.
nodes.norm_label: a6 — export is the only (one-way, unlabeled) unit conversion

nodes.label: A7 — Imprecise lb-to-kg divisor
nodes.rationale: ExportView uses 2.20462 instead of the exact 0.45359237 kg/lb definition; ~0.9 ppm error, irrelevant at current display resolution but avoidable.

nodes.label: A8 — todayISO returns UTC date, not local date
nodes.rationale: console-store.jsx todayISO() calls toISOString() which converts to UTC before slicing; in positive-UTC-offset zones the day rolls over up to 3h early, in negative-offset zones up to 4h late, corrupting hydration, notes and program-day boundaries.
nodes.norm_label: a8 — todayiso returns utc date, not local date

nodes.label: A9 — isoDaysBetween loses a day across spring-forward DST
nodes.rationale: Parses 'YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00' as local midnight then divides the ms difference by 86400000; a spring-forward transition between the two dates makes the true elapsed interval 1h short, floor()-ing the day count down by one for the rest of the program.
nodes.norm_label: a9 — isodaysbetween loses a day across spring-forward dst

nodes.label: A10 — isoOffset returns previous day in positive-UTC-offset zones
nodes.rationale: Parses local midnight, adds days, then formats via toISOString() (UTC) - an identity call shifts the date back one day. Currently latent: the function is exported but never called anywhere in the codebase.
nodes.norm_label: a10 — isooffset returns previous day in positive-utc-offset zones

nodes.label: A11 — Program advances on wall-clock time alone; skipped days unrecoverable
nodes.rationale: programPosition is a pure function of (startDate, today) with no attendance/pause/cursor input; a 10-day travel gap after 3 training days silently skips to day 14, with days 4-13 unreachable except by manual scrubbing.
nodes.norm_label: a11 — program advances on wall-clock time alone; skipped days unrecoverable

nodes.label: A12 — Before-start/after-end branches produce unread plausible-wrong states
nodes.rationale: The days<0 and days>=168 branches set .future/.past flags that grep confirms no consumer reads; a future start date renders as day 1 today, and day 168+ pins permanently to the Full Rest day at 100% progress.
nodes.norm_label: a12 — before-start/after-end branches produce unread plausible-wrong states

nodes.label: A13 — Program position never recomputed at midnight
nodes.rationale: programPosition runs inside a useMemo keyed on `[s]`, which does not change on a clock tick; an app left open across midnight keeps showing yesterday's session until some state write or reload occurs.
nodes.norm_label: a13 — program position never recomputed at midnight

nodes.label: A14 — Week/day auto-sync effect has incomplete dependencies
nodes.rationale: The sync effect depends on [s.startDate, s.view]; pressing 'j' to change s.week while on TODAY does not re-trigger it, so TODAY renders a different week's session under the 'today is...' heading.
nodes.norm_label: a14 — week/day auto-sync effect has incomplete dependencies

nodes.label: A15 — 'Monday' weigh-in trigger is calendar Monday, not program week
nodes.rationale: isMon checks the real-world day of week, unrelated to the program's startDate+7n week boundary; for a Thursday-start user the MONDAY weigh-in prompt appears mid-week and files under the currently-selected week.
nodes.norm_label: a15 — 'monday' weigh-in trigger is calendar monday, not program week

nodes.label: A16 — setsForWeek returns a 2-set target for exercises with no set count
nodes.rationale: parseInt(ex.sets) on the '-' sentinel (used for Light walk, Rower intervals, Stair climber, No training) yields NaN which is coerced to 2, so ComplianceGrid marks every rest day of all 24 weeks as permanently non-compliant.
nodes.norm_label: a16 — setsforweek returns a 2-set target for exercises with no set count

nodes.label: A17 — setsForWeek ignores weekly volume ramp for fixed-count exercises
nodes.rationale: Only the 'lo->hi' range branch clamps against vol.sets; plain-integer set counts (e.g. Face pulls: 3) do not drop during the volume ramp, so two incompatible volume policies coexist in one session.
nodes.norm_label: a17 — setsforweek ignores weekly volume ramp for fixed-count exercises

nodes.label: A18 — Deload override silently overwrites custom exercise set counts
nodes.rationale: `if (vol.deload) return 2;` fires before checking custom exercises, so a user-authored custom exercise with sets:'5' renders a target of 2 during deload weeks (6,12,18,24), ignoring what the user asked for.
nodes.norm_label: a18 — deload override silently overwrites custom exercise set counts

nodes.label: A19 — parseReps treats durations as repetitions
nodes.rationale: A regex/parseInt applied to a free-text field yields e.g. {lo:60,hi:60} for a 60-second Plank hold and {lo:20,hi:30} for a 20-30 min walk, so downstream suggestedLoad and makeCoachLine treat seconds/minutes as rep counts.
nodes.norm_label: a19 — parsereps treats durations as repetitions

nodes.label: A20 — 'max' disables load progression instead of triggering AMRAP handling
nodes.rationale: parseReps('max') returns null, which is coerced to hi=99, so the >=99 test at console-store.jsx:251 for progression never fires; Pull-ups and Push-ups silently never get the +2.5 progression, with no error shown.
nodes.norm_label: a20 — 'max' disables load progression instead of triggering amrap handling

nodes.label: A21 — Three separator conventions across two parsers, none validated
nodes.rationale: data.js uses en dash for rep ranges, AddCustomExercise defaults to ASCII hyphen, and setsForWeek requires an arrow; parseReps happens to accept both dash forms but nothing validates the source data.
nodes.norm_label: a21 — three separator conventions across two parsers, none validated

nodes.label: A22 — suggestedLoad uses last 2 sets, not last 2 sessions
nodes.rationale: Despite a comment describing a 2-session rule, hitTop checks matches.slice(0,2) over all sets sorted only by timestamp with no grouping by (week, day); two sets within one session can trigger next-session's load bump immediately.
nodes.norm_label: a22 — suggestedload uses last 2 sets, not last 2 sessions

nodes.label: A23 — suggestedLoad has no week/session boundary; scrubbing corrupts suggestion
nodes.rationale: Iterates all of s.sets ordered by wall-clock ts, which disagrees with program time; scrubbing ahead to log a trial set makes that set 'newest' and corrupts the suggestion for the week the user actually returns to. The sibling lastLoggedSet filters by (wk,d) correctly but still ranks by ts.
nodes.norm_label: a23 — suggestedload has no week/session boundary; scrubbing corrupts suggestion

nodes.label: A24 — Exact float equality gates the progression rule
nodes.rationale: `m.weight === last.weight` breaks silently on any floating-point drift from a future kg/lb conversion or inconsistent decimal entry; should compare within a tolerance tied to the plate increment.
nodes.norm_label: a24 — exact float equality gates the progression rule

nodes.label: A25 — makeCoachLine's PR branch compares weight only, ignoring reps/unit
nodes.rationale: A single-rep grinder is announced as a weight PR over a clean higher-volume set; the same lastBest object then feeds buildTelemetryMsg's e1RM/PR messages under a different, overall-record interpretation of the same data.
nodes.norm_label: a25 — makecoachline's pr branch compares weight only, ignoring reps/unit

nodes.label: A26 — Positional custom-exercise indices re-attribute sets on delete
nodes.rationale: Custom exercises use exIdx = 1000+i (an array position); removeCustomExercise filters by index, so deleting one exercise shifts the array and makes the next one inherit the deleted exercise's exIdx and displayed logged sets, orphaning the true owner's rows permanently.
nodes.norm_label: a26 — positional custom-exercise indices re-attribute sets on delete

nodes.label: A27 — Custom exercises logged but never counted
nodes.rationale: derived.exCount/setsTarget, ComplianceGrid and the streak scan all iterate day.exercises only, excluding custom exercises, while their logged sets do increment totalSetsLogged - the two counters disagree by construction.
nodes.norm_label: a27 — custom exercises logged but never counted

nodes.label: A28 — Derived context frozen into every persisted set
nodes.rationale: Each stored set carries exName, both rep-range bounds, and the suggestion and lifetime-best objects as they stood at log time; these are recomputable and go stale immediately, roughly a 5x multiplier on the largest table against a localStorage quota that fails silently.
nodes.norm_label: a28 — derived context frozen into every persisted set

nodes.label: A29 — RestTimer AudioContext constructed inside timer callback, never unlocked
nodes.rationale: `new AudioContext()` runs inside the setInterval handler rather than a user-gesture click handler and ctx.resume() is never called; on Safari/iOS and gesture-less Chrome the oscillator is scheduled and the context closed 600ms later with no sound ever produced.
nodes.norm_label: a29 — resttimer audiocontext constructed inside timer callback, never unlocked

nodes.label: A30 — navigator.vibrate haptic fallback unsupported on iOS
nodes.rationale: navigator.vibrate is not implemented in Safari on iOS/iPadOS; combined with A29, the rest timer's completion signal on an iPhone is silent, haptic-free, and visual-only on a screen that may be off.
nodes.norm_label: a30 — navigator.vibrate haptic fallback unsupported on ios

nodes.label: A31 — Timer chime check frozen while tab backgrounded, fires late on return
nodes.rationale: The elapsed-time computation is wall-clock correct, but the chime test lives inside the same throttled/suspended interval callback; locking the phone mid-rest and unlocking after the target has passed plays the chime tens of seconds late.
nodes.norm_label: a31 — timer chime check frozen while tab backgrounded, fires late on return

nodes.label: A32 — RestTimer is component-local, destroyed by any navigation
nodes.rationale: RestTimer is rendered inside TrainView and App swaps views by conditional render (unmounting it); navigating away mid-rest discards running/elapsed/startedAt state with no warning, and it is not tied to a specific set.
nodes.norm_label: a32 — resttimer is component-local, destroyed by any navigation

nodes.label: A33 — Rest timer overtime is unbounded and display format flips
nodes.rationale: Once elapsed exceeds target, the progress ring pins at 100% and the label switches to a '+Ns' format with no auto-stop or upper bound; a timer left running overnight displays absurd values like +43200s.
nodes.norm_label: a33 — rest timer overtime is unbounded and display format flips

nodes.label: A34 — Hydration target is a fixed cup count with volume only implied in a label
nodes.rationale: waterTarget is a dimensionless integer (7); the 500 mL-per-cup figure exists only in heading/tooltip strings, is read-only, and does not scale to body mass, training load, or climate.
nodes.norm_label: a34 — hydration target is a fixed cup count with volume only implied in a label

nodes.label: A35 — Hydration day boundary is UTC (compounds A8)
nodes.rationale: Hydration cups and the daily note and meal tracker are all keyed by todayISO(), so cups tapped at 01:00 local in a positive-offset timezone credit to the previous calendar day and the grid resets at 03:00 rather than midnight.
nodes.norm_label: a35 — hydration day boundary is utc (compounds a8)

nodes.label: A36 — Cup control cannot express a partial or non-monotonic day
nodes.rationale: Tapping cup i sets the count to i+1, always a prefix; combined with a single integer per day this makes it impossible to record timing, which a hydration cue (a stated new requirement) needs.
nodes.norm_label: a36 — cup control cannot express a partial or non-monotonic day

nodes.label: A37 — Streak reads 0 for the whole day until the first set is logged
nodes.rationale: The streak loop starts at back=0 (today) and breaks on the first non-compliant day; on a day with 20 consecutive prior compliant days but no set logged yet, the streak displays 0 at exactly the moment it would motivate the user.
nodes.norm_label: a37 — streak reads 0 for the whole day until the first set is logged

nodes.label: A38 — Rest days counted compliant on weak, inconsistent grounds
nodes.rationale: Day 7 is unconditionally compliant; day 4 is compliant if a push-up value exists anywhere in that week because pushupLog is keyed by week not day, so one Monday entry marks the whole week's rest days compliant, while cardio days get no such exemption.
nodes.norm_label: a38 — rest days counted compliant on weak, inconsistent grounds

nodes.label: A39 — Streak window capped at 30 days with no indication
nodes.rationale: The streak loop bounds at back<30; a 60-day streak displays as 30 and stops growing, a ceiling reached before the halfway point of a 168-day program.
nodes.norm_label: a39 — streak window capped at 30 days with no indication

nodes.label: A40 — s.streak is dead state
nodes.rationale: defaultState() declares streak:{last,count} but grep finds no reader or writer; the live value shown is the derived streakCount instead.

nodes.label: A41 — Every state change writes the entire store to localStorage synchronously
nodes.rationale: A useEffect keyed on [s] serialises and writes the whole state on every keystroke in a note or meal field, on the main thread, against a store with ~7 fields per set across up to ~2,400 sets, while also re-running the 30-day streak and whole-log plateau scans.
nodes.norm_label: a41 — every state change writes the entire store to localstorage synchronously

nodes.label: A42 — localStorage quota failure is swallowed silently
nodes.rationale: setItem is wrapped in try/catch(e){}; once the ~5MB origin quota is exceeded every subsequent write throws QuotaExceededError, is discarded, and the app keeps rendering healthy-looking in-memory state until the next reload reveals the loss.
nodes.norm_label: a42 — localstorage quota failure is swallowed silently

nodes.label: A43 — Import races the persistence effect and can be silently overwritten
nodes.rationale: The import flow writes localStorage directly (bypassing the store) then waits 800ms before reload; any setS during that window (toast timers, SW update toast, auto-sync effect) re-fires the store's own persistence effect and overwrites the imported snapshot with pre-import state, while still reporting success.
nodes.norm_label: a43 — import races the persistence effect and can be silently overwritten

nodes.label: A44 — One-tap irreversible wipe with no confirmation on every screen
nodes.rationale: A footer button labelled '$ rm -rf logs/', rendered on every view, calls localStorage.removeItem + reload with zero confirmation, unlike the sibling reset path which does prompt.
nodes.norm_label: a44 — one-tap irreversible wipe with no confirmation on every screen

nodes.label: A45 — defaultState() is not the real state shape
nodes.rationale: Four fields the app actually writes (customEx, mealsByDay, skipped, lastDeletedSet) are absent from defaultState(), so the import merge cannot supply defaults for them and every consumer must guard individually or crash.
nodes.norm_label: a45 — defaultstate() is not the real state shape

nodes.label: A46 — logSet computes wasNew from a stale render closure
nodes.rationale: wasNew is read from the outer render's `s` rather than the updater argument; two logSet calls in the same React batch both see wasNew=true and the side-effect block (counter increment, RNG roll, milestone check) runs twice for one set, potentially stepping over and permanently losing a milestone. clearSet has the same defect.
nodes.norm_label: a46 — logset computes wasnew from a stale render closure

nodes.label: A47 — totalSetsLogged only ever increases
nodes.rationale: clearSet removes a set but never decrements the counter; a log-delete-log cycle inflates the count so milestone toasts fire against a number that disagrees with the actual number of stored sets shown in the export.

nodes.label: A48 — Whole app re-renders on every write
nodes.rationale: A single useState object is passed as one prop into every view with no memoisation, so every descendant re-renders on each keystroke; ComplianceGrid compounds this with an O(n) find inside a nested render loop (~14,000 comparisons per render) plus a dead no-op statement.
nodes.norm_label: a48 — whole app re-renders on every write

nodes.label: A49 — Tweaks never persist; the store's own tweak plumbing is dead
nodes.rationale: useTweaks posts to window.parent (a design-canvas host protocol) which goes nowhere in the deployed PWA since window.parent===window; meanwhile defaultState().tweaks and the store's own setTweak exist, are exported, and have no reader.
nodes.norm_label: a49 — tweaks never persist; the store's own tweak plumbing is dead

nodes.label: A50 — App functions only because Babel downlevels const to global var
nodes.rationale: Babel-standalone's script-tag runner injects each transformed file as a classic <script> sharing one global scope, and default preset-env with no browser targets compiles to ES5 so top-level const/let become var and redeclaration is legal; eight .jsx files each open with a top-level `const {useState,...}=React`. If that downlevelling ever stops, the second script to load throws a redeclaration SyntaxError and the page renders black - the documented mechanism behind past black-screen-after-deploy incidents.
nodes.norm_label: a50 — app functions only because babel downlevels const to global var

nodes.label: A51 — Live global-name collision on STORE_KEY
nodes.rationale: core.jsx and console-video.jsx both declare a top-level `const STORE_KEY` in the shared global scope created by A50; console-video.jsx loads later so its value wins, meaning core.jsx's loadStore/saveStore would silently read/write the video-instance key the moment anything calls them.
nodes.norm_label: a51 — live global-name collision on store_key

nodes.label: A52 — Conditionally-called React hook
nodes.rationale: `if (window.useKonamiCode) window.useKonamiCode(...)` calls useRef/useEffect internally - a Rules-of-Hooks violation whose hook count depends on a runtime condition, surviving only because load order is currently deterministic.

nodes.label: A53 — Modal-handle effect re-runs every render and briefly nulls handles
nodes.rationale: The effect's dependency array holds fresh object literals from useVideoModal/useFormCuesModal on every render, so it never compares equal; the cleanup nulls window.__videoModal and the effect immediately resets it, leaving the handle null on first paint when ExerciseCard reads it during render.
nodes.norm_label: a53 — modal-handle effect re-runs every render and briefly nulls handles

nodes.label: A54 — Two keydown listeners bind the same key
nodes.rationale: A global handler and TrainView's handler both bind 'j' to window with neither stopping propagation; pressing 'j' on TRAIN with no input focused both opens the next exercise and advances the program week by one.
nodes.norm_label: a54 — two keydown listeners bind the same key

nodes.label: A55 — Cross-file exports incomplete; app relies on implicit window globals
nodes.rationale: console-fun.jsx exports only a handful of names, yet other files call window.buildTelemetryMsg, window.useKonamiCode, window.useFormCuesModal and window.TimeCapsule, none of which appear in any explicit export - they resolve only because top-level function declarations in a classic script land on window (A50), and each becomes silently undefined under module semantics.
nodes.norm_label: a55 — cross-file exports incomplete; app relies on implicit window globals

nodes.label: A56 — Production ships React development builds and an in-browser compiler
nodes.rationale: index.html loads react.development.js, react-dom.development.js and @babel/standalone (~3MB uncompressed), all cached by the service worker; every page load parses and compiles nine .jsx files in-browser, contrary to Babel's own documented guidance against production use of @babel/standalone.
nodes.norm_label: a56 — production ships react development builds and an in-browser compiler

nodes.label: A57 — Specimen drop RNG runs inside a non-idempotent state updater
nodes.rationale: Math.random() is evaluated inside a React state updater function, which may be invoked more than once per dispatch (e.g. under StrictMode), making the same dispatch capable of yielding different state.
nodes.norm_label: a57 — specimen drop rng runs inside a non-idempotent state updater

nodes.label: A58 — Drop rarity flattens as the collection fills; pool exhausts early
nodes.rationale: drawSpecimen draws without replacement from a 42-card pool (common:uncommon:rare weighted 6:3:1) at 15% per qualifying set; at typical weekly volume the pool exhausts within about a month, after which the entire mechanic goes dead for the remaining ~20 weeks.
nodes.norm_label: a58 — drop rarity flattens as the collection fills; pool exhausts early

nodes.label: A59 — An undismissed specimen drop is silently replaced
nodes.rationale: next.lastDrop unconditionally overwrites any pending lastDrop; a second drop within the 12-second auto-dismiss window replaces the first card, which the user never sees, even though it is still credited to the collection.
nodes.norm_label: a59 — an undismissed specimen drop is silently replaced

nodes.label: A60 — Bodyweight and timed work cannot be logged as a real set at all
nodes.rationale: The wasNew gate and makeCoachLine's null-return both treat `0` as falsy; Pull-ups, Push-ups and Plank logged at 0 kg produce no coach line, no telemetry, no specimen roll, and no counter increment, while the UI still shows the row as logged with no signal that it was treated differently.
nodes.norm_label: a60 — bodyweight and timed work cannot be logged as a real set at all

nodes.label: A61 — Phase-transition cutscene keyed to scrubbed week, not program position
nodes.rationale: The cutscene's trigger reads derived.phase.n, which derives from the scrub-position s.week rather than the true program position; scrubbing ahead to look at week 20 fires the cutscene early and marks it seen, permanently disabling the real transitions at weeks 9 and 17.
nodes.norm_label: a61 — phase-transition cutscene keyed to scrubbed week, not program position

nodes.label: A62 — SkipSession writes to a key nothing reads
nodes.rationale: s.skipped is written but grep confirms no reader anywhere in the codebase; the button changes no visible state, does not exempt the day from the streak or heatmap, cannot be undone, and disappears once anything is logged.
nodes.norm_label: a62 — skipsession writes to a key nothing reads

nodes.label: A63 — 'Done' has three incompatible definitions
nodes.rationale: A manual completed[] boolean toggle, a setsLogged>=target derivation, and the heatmap's own intensity ratio disagree; a user who logs every set without touching the manual toggle sees '0/5 exercises' beside '20/20 sets' and never gets the ALL DONE badge, while ExerciseCard independently shows the card as complete.

nodes.label: A64 — pushupLog[wk] carries two contradictory meanings
nodes.rationale: Declared and exported as a weekly max, but PushupTodayCard treats it as a running daily tally (+1/+5) while PushupQuickLog overwrites it with an absolute max, so a true max entered later in the week destroys an earlier daily tally.
nodes.norm_label: a64 — pushuplog[wk] carries two contradictory meanings

nodes.label: A65 — PWA update toast unreachable because the worker skips waiting at install
nodes.rationale: sw.js calls self.skipWaiting() during install, so the worker never sits in the 'waiting' state the primary detection branch checks for; by the time the secondary statechange branch catches 'installed', SKIP_WAITING postMessage is a no-op against an already-active worker, producing a version-skew window with an unreliable update prompt.
nodes.norm_label: a65 — pwa update toast unreachable because the worker skips waiting at install

nodes.label: A66 — Install step swallows 404s so a partial deploy caches silently
nodes.rationale: Promise.all(SHELL.map(u => c.add(u).catch(() => null))) lets a missing/mistyped file install 'successfully' with a hole in the shell; the cache-first fetch handler then serves a stale copy indefinitely until CACHE_NAME is bumped by hand.
nodes.norm_label: a66 — install step swallows 404s so a partial deploy caches silently

nodes.label: A67 — manifest.json, CSS and TWEAK_DEFAULTS disagree on theme colour
nodes.rationale: Three different accent colours are declared: manifest.json/index.html theme_color #00ff88, index.html CSS --accent #a3e635, and console-app.jsx TWEAK_DEFAULTS.accent #f472b6.
nodes.norm_label: a67 — manifest.json, css and tweak_defaults disagree on theme colour

nodes.label: A68 — Boot sequence hard-codes one subject's anthropometry
nodes.rationale: The boot screen prints a specific mass, body-fat percentage, lean mass and target as if universal - the first screen a new user of a multi-user build would see.
nodes.norm_label: a68 — boot sequence hard-codes one subject's anthropometry

nodes.label: A69 — Export snapshot includes transient UI state
nodes.rationale: dlJson serialises the whole of s including lastDrop, lastTelemetry, lastMilestone and lastDeletedSet; re-importing replays a stale toast on first render.
nodes.norm_label: a69 — export snapshot includes transient ui state

nodes.label: A70 — String/number comparison in the export delta sign logic
nodes.rationale: `delta > 0 ? '+' : ''` compares a string (toFixed(1) result) to a number; works only by JS coercion and would not survive an unmodified TypeScript port.
nodes.norm_label: a70 — string/number comparison in the export delta sign logic

nodes.label: A71 — Video modal only persists a working instance via the external-link click
nodes.rationale: markInstanceWorking is wired solely to the 'open in new tab' anchor's onClick; a user for whom the embedded iframe works perfectly and never leaves the app re-tries the same failing instance every time.
nodes.norm_label: a71 — video modal only persists a working instance via the external-link click

nodes.label: A72 — Nav/hotkey documentation drift
nodes.rationale: VIEWS has seven entries and the in-app help panel says '1-7', while DEPLOY.md documents Export as item 6.

nodes.label: Kg (type)
nodes.rationale: Kilograms, non-negative, canonical mass unit; never rounded on write.

nodes.label: ML (type)
nodes.rationale: Millilitres, non-negative integer; canonical hydration volume unit.

nodes.label: Seconds (type)
nodes.rationale: Non-negative seconds; canonical duration unit.

nodes.label: EpochMs (type)
nodes.rationale: Epoch milliseconds, UTC; canonical instant representation.

nodes.label: LocalDate (type)
nodes.rationale: Calendar day in the user's own timezone ('YYYY-MM-DD'), produced via Intl.DateTimeFormat with an explicit IANA zone - never via Date.prototype.toISOString(), which yields the UTC day and shifts the boundary by the offset.

nodes.label: LocalTime (type)
nodes.rationale: Wall-clock time of day in the user's timezone ('HH:mm').

nodes.label: TimeZone (type)
nodes.rationale: IANA zone id (e.g. 'Europe/Athens'); required on the profile, never inferred silently.

nodes.label: IsoWeekday (type)
nodes.rationale: 1=Monday...7=Sunday, ISO-8601 weekday numbering.

nodes.label: UnitSystem (type)
nodes.rationale: 'metric' | 'imperial' - a display and input property of the profile only; storage stays SI regardless.

nodes.label: KG_PER_LB constant
nodes.rationale: Exact conversion factor 0.45359237 kg/lb, replacing the current codebase's approximate 2.20462 divisor.

nodes.label: LOAD_INCREMENT constant
nodes.rationale: Smallest assemblable plate increment per unit system: 1.25 kg (metric) or 2.5 lb (imperial), replacing the current unconditional +2.5.

nodes.label: Profile
nodes.rationale: One per user; a deployment holds many. Carries timezone, unit system, body baseline/target and hydration target - none of which exist in the current single-user, single-subject state shape.

nodes.label: AvailabilitySlot
nodes.rationale: One weekday + start time + expected duration; replaces the implicit 7-consecutive-calendar-day rotation with an explicit weekly schedule.

nodes.label: Availability
nodes.rationale: The set of AvailabilitySlots plus a weeklySessionTarget, driving miss detection for the weekly review.

nodes.label: Prescription
nodes.rationale: Typed discriminated union (reps/amrap/time/distance/duration/none) replacing the free-text '6-8'/'60 s'/'-' strings that parseReps currently mis-parses.

nodes.label: Exercise
nodes.rationale: A stable-id exercise definition with an explicit isBodyweight flag and a videoQuery search string instead of a fragile video id.

nodes.label: PlannedExercise
nodes.rationale: A resolved setsLo/setsHi integer pair plus a Prescription for one exercise within a planned session, replacing setsForWeek's ad hoc string parsing.

nodes.label: PlannedSession
nodes.rationale: A named, kinded (lift/cardio/rest), ordered session containing PlannedExercises.

nodes.label: PlanTemplate
nodes.rationale: A versioned, ordered sequence of PlannedSessions plus per-block volume/deload modifiers; a template decoupled from any calendar.

nodes.label: PlanCursor
nodes.rationale: Tracks nextSessionIndex into a PlanTemplate, advancing only when a session is completed or explicitly skipped - never on a calendar tick. Explicitly named as the fix for the current calendar-only program position.

nodes.label: PlanPause
nodes.rationale: A from/to interval marking a suspended stretch (illness, holiday), distinguishing a pause from a run of missed sessions.

nodes.label: SessionAssignment
nodes.rationale: One calendar day's chosen session plus status (planned/in-progress/completed/skipped/paused), letting a user pick or reorder today's session without touching the cursor sequence.

nodes.label: LoggedSet
nodes.rationale: A uuid-keyed logged set record with a nullable loadKg (0 valid for bodyweight, null for not-recorded) and enteredUnit, replacing the composite 'wk-day-ex-set' string key and the frozen derived-context fields.

nodes.label: BodyMassEntry
nodes.rationale: A per-profile, per-local-date body mass record in kg with enteredUnit, replacing the untyped lb-only weightLog.

nodes.label: HydrationEntry
nodes.rationale: A per-profile, per-local-date volumeML plus timestamped marks, replacing the dimensionless UTC-keyed cup count.

nodes.label: PushSubscriptionRecord
nodes.rationale: Web Push subscription (endpoint, keys, timezone) needed for the reminder system the current build has none of.

nodes.label: ReminderRule
nodes.rationale: A per-profile reminder schedule (session/hydration/weigh-in/weekly-review kind, lead time, active window, weekdays).

nodes.label: ReminderDelivery
nodes.rationale: An idempotency-guarded delivery record for one scheduled reminder instant.

nodes.label: WeeklyReview
nodes.rationale: Per-profile, per-ISO-week completed/target/skipped/paused tally with a signed delta, the missing weekly aggregate and miss-detection boundary the motivational-video trigger needs.

nodes.label: MotivationalAsset
nodes.rationale: A locally-hosted motivational video clip (src, poster, duration), contrasted with console-video.jsx's external Invidious-instance form-cue videos.

nodes.label: MotivationVideoState
nodes.rationale: Tracks lastShownForWeek/lastShownAt/recentAssetIds to prevent replay on every render or reload and to rotate clips.

nodes.label: AppState
nodes.rationale: The proposed root state shape with an explicit schemaVersion and per-profile records for every domain object, replacing defaultState()'s single flat single-user object.

nodes.label: displayLoad()
nodes.rationale: kg -> display value quantised to the plate increment; the only place a load unit conversion is allowed, contrasted with the export being the current build's sole (and unlabeled) conversion site.

nodes.label: toStoredLoad()
nodes.rationale: Entered display value -> exact kg for storage; never pre-rounds the input, preserving a lossless round trip via enteredUnit.

nodes.label: displayMass()
nodes.rationale: kg -> display value at 0.1 resolution with no plate quantisation, for body mass display.

nodes.label: nextLoad()
nodes.rationale: Progression step expressed in the user's own unit increment (1.25 kg or 2.5 lb), replacing the current codebase's flat, unit-blind +2.5 increment.

nodes.label: Content Peer Review — FixThisInjustice Training App (2026-09-01)
nodes.rationale: Scientific-content-only peer review of a personal 24-week WEC-unrelated fitness app being generalised from one named individual to a group. 103 tallied verdict rows across nutrition, training, hydration, supplements, 42 specimen cards, and form cues: 11 SUPPORTED, 33 PARTIALLY, 10 UNSUPPORTED, 46 WRONG, 3 COULD NOT VERIFY. Two commonly-circulated DOIs confirmed 404 and corrected: Grgic 2017 and de Salles 2009. Method: six parallel verification agents, 415 logged source fetches in REFERENCES.md.
nodes.norm_label: content peer review — fixthisinjustice training app (2026-09-01)

nodes.label: Section 2.1: Training Programming Review (Split, Volume, Frequency)
nodes.norm_label: section 2.1: training programming review (split, volume, frequency)

nodes.label: Weight curve endpoint contradicts stated target (WRONG)
nodes.rationale: data.js:70-74 24-week curve ends at 183.2 lb; stated target (data.js:11-13) is 174 lb, 9.2 lb (4.2 kg) short. Two mutually inconsistent endpoints in one file.
nodes.norm_label: weight curve endpoint contradicts stated target (wrong)

nodes.label: Taper mechanism claim is physiologically backwards (WRONG)
nodes.rationale: data.js:68-69 claims the plan 'tapers as TDEE rises'; TDEE falls during a 12 kg weight loss (lower mass/RMR/activity cost plus adaptive thermogenesis, Trexler/Smith-Ryan/Norton 2014). The stated mechanism is inverted.
nodes.norm_label: taper mechanism claim is physiologically backwards (wrong)

nodes.label: Phase-2 bench milestone is arithmetically impossible under the app's own progression rule (WRONG)
nodes.rationale: Using the app's own +2.5 kg/week rule with bench trained once weekly, Phase 2 needs +20 kg but the ceiling is +17.5 kg — infeasible even with a perfect streak in a caloric deficit with a week-12 deload.
nodes.norm_label: phase-2 bench milestone is arithmetically impossible under the app's own progression rule (wrong)

nodes.label: 'Upper Power' day mislabelled — first exercise is a lower-body lift (WRONG terminology)
nodes.rationale: data.js:170-183 Day 5 named 'Upper Power' opens with the trap-bar/conventional deadlift, a hip/knee-extension lower-body lift that also gives quads/hamstrings their only second weekly exposure — the mislabel hides the programme's real structure.
nodes.norm_label: 'upper power' day mislabelled — first exercise is a lower-body lift (wrong terminology)

nodes.label: Weekly direct-set volume and frequency for four muscle groups fall below evidence floors (WRONG)
nodes.rationale: Week-9 primary-mover count: biceps 5, calves 4, rear delt 3, side delt 3 sets/week, all trained only 1x/week. Currier 2026 ACSM Position Stand: hypertrophy enhanced by >=10 sets/wk; Currier 2023 BJSM network meta-analysis ranks twice-weekly multiset training highest (SMD 0.66).
nodes.norm_label: weekly direct-set volume and frequency for four muscle groups fall below evidence floors (wrong)

nodes.label: Flat +2.5 kg progression increment violates the 2-10% guideline band at both ends (WRONG)
nodes.rationale: console-store.jsx:252; console-train.jsx:129 step='2.5' applies the same increment to every exercise: 1.7% of a 150 kg squat (too small) and 12.5% of a 20 kg curl (above ACSM's 10% ceiling, unachievable without micro-plates).
nodes.norm_label: flat +2.5 kg progression increment violates the 2-10% guideline band at both ends (wrong)

nodes.label: Progression engine contains two internal rule/implementation mismatches (WRONG)
nodes.rationale: (1) Comment says 'last 2 sessions' but code takes matches.slice(0,2) by timestamp, so two top-range sets inside ONE session satisfy the condition — roughly twice as aggressive as documented. (2) Coach copy promises '+2.5 kg next session' after one top-range set while the engine requires two entries — the app promises a load increase it will not grant.
nodes.norm_label: progression engine contains two internal rule/implementation mismatches (wrong)

nodes.label: Deload load reduction is never applied, and the direction is backwards (WRONG)
nodes.rationale: data.js:248 / console-train.jsx:379 says 'Reduce weight by 40%'; only the set cut is implemented (setsForWeek returns 2) — the load cut exists only as a banner string, and suggestedLoad is deload-blind so it proposes resuming at the reduced load. Direction is also wrong: Bosquet 2007 meta-analysis found optimal taper decreases volume 41-60% WITHOUT modifying intensity. Deload extras ('No cardio', 'Eat 200 kcal more', data.js:249-250) are UNSUPPORTED and internally contradictory (adds intake, removes expenditure, against a fat-loss goal).
nodes.norm_label: deload load reduction is never applied, and the direction is backwards (wrong)

nodes.label: Fixed deload cadence (weeks 6/12/18/24) is UNSUPPORTED by the deload literature
nodes.rationale: Bell 2023 Delphi consensus: 100% panel agreement that deload frequency 'may depend on how athlete responds'; regular pre-planned deloads 'might not be necessary'. Coleman 2024: a mid-programme deload produced no hypertrophy benefit and the continuous group gained MORE lower-body strength.
nodes.norm_label: fixed deload cadence (weeks 6/12/18/24) is unsupported by the deload literature

nodes.label: Rest-timer default is too short and scoped incorrectly (WRONG)
nodes.rationale: console-train.jsx:7,371 defaults to 90 s (+60 s on 'heavy' days) against three sources placing heavy-compound rest above 90 s (de Salles 2009: 3-5 min; Grgic 2018: >2 min trained; Schoenfeld 2016: 3 min beat 1 min for 1RM squat/bench/quad thickness). Scoping is also wrong: isHeavyDay flags the whole day if it contains ANY compound, so 150 s gets applied to lateral raises and hammer curls on a compound day, with no per-exercise differentiation (console-train.jsx:324,371).
nodes.norm_label: rest-timer default is too short and scoped incorrectly (wrong)

nodes.label: Plateau-detection band (±1.0 lb over 3 points) is far narrower than natural weight noise (WRONG)
nodes.rationale: console-store.jsx:315-323. Bhutani 2017: 2-week weight change in weight-stable adults was 0.26 +/- 1.2 kg SD — 2.6x the app's entire 0.45 kg band, so the rule almost never fires, and when it does it has selected an unusually quiet stretch rather than a real stall. Orsama 2014: weight peaks Sun/Mon and falls through the week, so which weekdays the three readings land on can manufacture or erase a plateau.
nodes.norm_label: plateau-detection band (±1.0 lb over 3 points) is far narrower than natural weight noise (wrong)

nodes.label: Plateau response (150 kcal cut, wait 2 weeks) cannot resolve its own signal from noise
nodes.rationale: data.js:260. 150 kcal/d x 14 d ~= 2,100 kcal ~= 0.27 kg expected change against Bhutani's 1.2 kg 2-week SD — the expected signal is about one quarter of the noise, so the rule re-fires and compounds cuts on the basis of nothing. A fixed 150 kcal is also not equivalent across users (5% of 3,000 kcal vs 10% of 1,500 kcal).
nodes.norm_label: plateau response (150 kcal cut, wait 2 weeks) cannot resolve its own signal from noise

nodes.label: Streak logic credits rest days with no actual logging (WRONG)
nodes.rationale: console-store.jsx:328-351. Day 7 is credited unconditionally (dy===7 forces any=true, line 347); day 4 is credited if a push-up count exists for that WEEK (pushupLog is keyed by week, not day). Two of seven days need no logging, so a streak can grow while the user trains nothing.
nodes.norm_label: streak logic credits rest days with no actual logging (wrong)

nodes.label: Specimen-card reward economy is broken: drop rate exhausts the library in ~3 weeks; rarity shares drift from stated percentages (WRONG)
nodes.rationale: console-store.jsx:184-189,374: at 15%/set, computed 10.5-13.3 drops/week means the 42-card library is exhausted in ~3.2 weeks of a 24-week programme — the reward loop is dead for ~87% of the plan. console-content.js:562,706-710: stated weights 6/3/1 over 15/15/12 cards give pool shares 61.2/30.6/8.2%, not the claimed 60/30/10; all three drift further as cards are removed without replacement.
nodes.norm_label: specimen-card reward economy is broken: drop rate exhausts the library in ~3 weeks; rarity shares drift from stated percentages (wrong)

nodes.label: Mixed unit system with no conversion or display preference (WRONG, unit hazard)
nodes.rationale: console-store.jsx:256-258,294,321; console-train.jsx:127-129. weight_curve_lb, logWeight(wk, lb) and the plateau band are all in lb; the load input is kg with step='2.5'; no lb-plate support exists.
nodes.norm_label: mixed unit system with no conversion or display preference (wrong, unit hazard)

nodes.label: Flat 3.5 L/day fluid target for everyone is WRONG and sex-invariant
nodes.rationale: data.js:286; console-store.jsx:95 (waterTarget: 7, hard-coded, no setter anywhere in the codebase); console-views.jsx:194. IOM 2005 AI for total water is 3.7 L/d men, 2.7 L/d women (beverages 3.0 L / 2.2 L, ~81%). A flat 3.5 L overshoots the female total AI by ~30% while undershooting the male, and cannot adapt to body mass, sex, climate or sweat rate.
nodes.norm_label: flat 3.5 l/day fluid target for everyone is wrong and sex-invariant

nodes.label: Intra-session '500 ml between sets' instruction has a route to acute harm (WRONG — highest-severity finding)
nodes.rationale: console-train.jsx:262-266. Week-9 computation: D5 Upper Power, 9 inter-set intervals -> 4.5 L in a single session, exceeding any plausible sweat rate or gastric-emptying rate, and self-contradictory against the app's own 3.5 L daily target. Sawka/ACSM 2007 prescribes no fixed volume, recommends weigh-in/weigh-out sweat-rate estimation, goal <2% body-weight loss. Over-drinking beyond sweat losses is the mechanism of exercise-associated hyponatraemia. Recommended: delete this instruction outright.
nodes.norm_label: intra-session '500 ml between sets' instruction has a route to acute harm (wrong — highest-severity finding)

nodes.label: Five-item supplement stack prescribed to all users with no screening (UNSUPPORTED)
nodes.rationale: data.js:234-240. No contraindication list, no interaction check, no age or pregnancy gating anywhere in the file.
nodes.norm_label: five-item supplement stack prescribed to all users with no screening (unsupported)

nodes.label: Magnesium glycinate top-of-range dose exceeds the supplemental UL (WRONG at the top of the range)
nodes.rationale: data.js:219,239: 200-400 mg PM. IOM 1997 tabulated UL for supplemental magnesium is 350 mg/d for all adults ('The ULs only include magnesium from dietary supplements and medications'); the app's 400 mg top end exceeds it by 14%. UL is set on elemental magnesium regardless of salt form.
nodes.norm_label: magnesium glycinate top-of-range dose exceeds the supplemental ul (wrong at the top of the range)

nodes.label: 2,000 IU/day vitamin D3 blanket prescription is an unsupported empiric dose (PARTIALLY — safe but unsupported as a default)
nodes.rationale: data.js:237, rationale 'Indoor PhD deficiency risk'. IOM 2011: RDA 600 IU, UL 4,000 IU, so 2,000 IU is within safety bounds, but Demay 2024 Endocrine Society guideline 'suggests against empiric vitamin D supplementation above the current DRI... in healthy adults younger than 75 years' without 25(OH)D testing.
nodes.norm_label: 2,000 iu/day vitamin d3 blanket prescription is an unsupported empiric dose (partially — safe but unsupported as a default)

nodes.label: No warm-up protocol, readiness screening, or contraindication language anywhere in the reviewed files (WRONG — omission)
nodes.rationale: Grep for warm.?up|par-?q|physician|contraindic|screen across all four reviewed files returns zero hits, despite prescribing 4-5 rep sets on barbell squats, deadlifts and presses.
nodes.norm_label: no warm-up protocol, readiness screening, or contraindication language anywhere in the reviewed files (wrong — omission)

nodes.label: Heavy row explicitly permits form breakdown ('cheat' reps) on the heaviest loaded hip-hinge (WRONG, unsafe)
nodes.rationale: console-content.js:409,424: 'you can use a slight cheat / TnT' at 5-6 reps — contradicts the same file's own mistake list ('Rounding lower back -> injury', line 420), for a population that includes novices.
nodes.norm_label: heavy row explicitly permits form breakdown ('cheat' reps) on the heaviest loaded hip-hinge (wrong, unsafe)

nodes.label: Form-cue lookup key mismatch silently drops cues for one exercise (WRONG, silent failure)
nodes.rationale: data.js:154 plan name 'Leg press -> Bulgarian split' vs console-content.js:266 FORM_CUES key 'Leg press -> Bulgarian split squat' — the lookup fails, so that exercise silently has no form cues (28 of 29 resolve).
nodes.norm_label: form-cue lookup key mismatch silently drops cues for one exercise (wrong, silent failure)

nodes.label: Setup screen collects only one field (programme start date) — nothing can be personalised (blocking problem)
nodes.rationale: console-shared.jsx Setup component. Grep confirms 'age', 'height', 'sex', 'female', 'male' appear nowhere in data.js, console-store.jsx or console-train.jsx except as SVG attributes and card prose. Every subject parameter (95.3 kg, 27% BF, 190 g protein, 2,350 kcal, 3.5 L, 65 kg starting bench) is a hard-coded literal in data.js.
nodes.norm_label: setup screen collects only one field (programme start date) — nothing can be personalised (blocking problem)

nodes.label: RPE 7-8 cap on compounds is defensible; the stated Vyvanse/caffeine rationale is invalid three ways (PARTIALLY — right cap, wrong reason)
nodes.rationale: data.js:285; console-train.jsx:207,264; console-store.jsx:394. Cap itself supported by Refalo 2023 (failure vs non-failure ES=0.19). Reason invalid: (i) Zourdos 2016 RIR-based RPE is validated against bar velocity, not cardiovascular strain; (ii) Doherty & Smith 2005 found caffeine REDUCES RPE by 5.6% — direction backwards; (iii) no trial of lisdexamfetamine on resistance-training RPE exists.
nodes.norm_label: rpe 7-8 cap on compounds is defensible; the stated vyvanse/caffeine rationale is invalid three ways (partially — right cap, wrong reason)

nodes.label: Daily energy and protein targets are literals derived from no stated equation and no user input (PARTIALLY)
nodes.rationale: data.js:26-27,41-42,56-57,232,271-272: 2,000-2,350 kcal and 190 g protein are hard-coded to one 95.3 kg subject; Mifflin-St Jeor requires height and age, which the app never collects. Energy also rises Phase 1->Phase 2 while body mass falls, shrinking the deficit twice over.
nodes.norm_label: daily energy and protein targets are literals derived from no stated equation and no user input (partially)

nodes.label: '10 sets/muscle/week is optimal' is a mis-cited category boundary, not an optimum (rejected framing)
nodes.rationale: Schoenfeld 2017's categorical model (<5/5-9/10+ sets) was P=0.074, not significant — routinely misreported as a finding. Currier 2026 ACSM's '>=10 sets/wk' is a floor, not an optimum; the true dose-response curve (Pelland 2025, Currier 2026) is monotonic increasing and decelerating with no identified plateau or optimum within the studied range.
nodes.norm_label: '10 sets/muscle/week is optimal' is a mis-cited category boundary, not an optimum (rejected framing)

nodes.label: Leg-press 90-degree ROM cap cue contradicts the app's own specimen card c010 on squat depth (PARTIALLY)
nodes.rationale: console-content.js:273,278 'Lower until knees ~90deg... STOP at 90deg' is arbitrary and contradicts card c010's own argument that full ROM is better for the knee. The real limit is lumbar flexion (pad peeling), which the cue already names.
nodes.norm_label: leg-press 90-degree rom cap cue contradicts the app's own specimen card c010 on squat depth (partially)

nodes.label: Mifflin-St Jeor RMR equation (default when body fat unknown)
nodes.rationale: RMR = 10*weight(kg)+6.25*height(cm)-5*age(y)+5 (male) / -161 (female). Adopted default: Frankenfield 2013 found it accurate in 82% overall (87% non-obese, 75% obese) and unbiased (95% CI -26 to +8 kcal/d) where other equations overestimated.
nodes.norm_label: mifflin-st jeor rmr equation (default when body fat unknown)

nodes.label: Cunningham (1991) FFM-based RMR equation (default when body fat is known)
nodes.rationale: RMR = 370 + 21.6*FFM(kg). Explains 65-90% of REE variation; validated most accurate of four equations in endurance athletes (Thompson & Manore 1996). Widely mislabelled 'Katch-McArdle'; Cunningham published it. Distinct from the earlier Cunningham 1980 equation (BMR=500+22*LBM) — do not conflate.
nodes.norm_label: cunningham (1991) ffm-based rmr equation (default when body fat is known)

nodes.label: Harris-Benedict / Roza-Shizgal RMR equation — REJECTED
nodes.rationale: Rejected in favor of Mifflin-St Jeor and Cunningham: Mifflin's own data showed Harris-Benedict overestimating REE by 5% (p<0.01); Frankenfield 2013 placed it among the overestimating equations; Roza's own precision is only +/-14%.

nodes.label: FAO/WHO/UNU (2004) activity/PAL bands — ADOPTED
nodes.rationale: PAL bands 1.40-1.69 (sedentary/light), 1.70-1.99 (active), 2.00-2.40 (vigorous), verified from the primary PDF and HTML chapter. NASEM 2023 offers an alternative (inactive<1.53/low<1.68/active<1.85/very active<2.50) but those cut-points are literally the 25th/50th/75th percentiles of its own dataset, not physiological thresholds, and NASEM 2023 abandoned BMR x PAL entirely.

nodes.label: Ubiquitous gym-ladder multipliers 1.2/1.375/1.55/1.725/1.9 — REJECTED
nodes.rationale: No primary source exists (Europe PMC search: 13 papers, earliest 2007, all downstream users with no citation). Values are an interpolated three-point scale (1.375=(1.2+1.55)/2, 1.725=(1.55+1.9)/2 exactly, by arithmetic). The 1.2 anchor traces to Black et al. 1996's non-ambulant (bedridden) limit, explicitly excluded from their free-living dataset; FAO's free-living floor is 1.40, so the gym scale systematically under-feeds sedentary users.

nodes.label: Fat-loss rate: 0.5-1.0 %BW/week, 0.7% best supported — ADOPTED
nodes.rationale: Garthe 2011: 0.7%/wk vs 1.4%/wk gave lean body mass +2.1+/-0.4% (slow) vs -0.2+/-0.7% (fast), between-group p<0.01, concluding athletes 'should aim for a weekly BW loss of 0.7%'. Helms 2014: 0.5-1%/wk to maximize muscle retention.

nodes.label: '3,500 kcal per pound' static energy-balance rule — REJECTED
nodes.rationale: Hall et al. 2011 (The Lancet): the static rule 'ignores dynamic physiological adaptations to altered body weight'. Replaced by a dynamic model.
nodes.norm_label: '3,500 kcal per pound' static energy-balance rule — rejected

nodes.label: Hall dynamic energy-balance replacement rule — ADOPTED replacement for the 3,500 kcal/lb rule
nodes.rationale: Verbatim: 'every permanent change of energy intake of 100 kJ per day will lead to an eventual weight change of about 1 kg (equivalently, 10 kcal per day per pound of weight change) and it will take about 1 year to achieve half of the total weight change.'
nodes.norm_label: hall dynamic energy-balance replacement rule — adopted replacement for the 3,500 kcal/lb rule

nodes.label: Muscle-gain surplus ~350-500 kcal/day — weakly evidenced, stated as such
nodes.rationale: Slater 2019: the specific surplus required for hypertrophy is 'unknown' and has 'never been validated' in a resistance-training population. The one measured figure, Garthe 2011 (surplus study): a counselled 506+/-84 kcal/d surplus with 4 sessions/wk gave LBM +2.8+/-0.5% vs ad-libitum controls with no LBM change.
nodes.norm_label: muscle-gain surplus ~350-500 kcal/day — weakly evidenced, stated as such

nodes.label: Protein targets with denominators kept strictly separate (BW vs FFM) — ADOPTED
nodes.rationale: Maintenance/gain: 1.4-2.2 g/kg BODY WEIGHT/day (Jager 2017 ISSN position stand, Morton 2018 meta-regression breakpoint ~1.62 g/kg, reported as non-significant segmental regression p=0.079 — do not present as a hard threshold). Fat loss in a deficit: 2.3-3.1 g/kg FAT-FREE MASS/day (Helms 2014). Unit trap: Jager's abstract prints 2.3-3.1 as bare g/kg/d inside a BW-convention document without citing Helms; applying it to body weight at 25% body fat is a ~33% overfeed.
nodes.norm_label: protein targets with denominators kept strictly separate (bw vs ffm) — adopted

nodes.label: 0.8 g/kg RDA protein floor — REJECTED
nodes.rationale: Jager 2017 verbatim: 'multiple lines of evidence indicating this value is not an appropriate amount for a training athlete'; in a 30% deficit the 1xRDA group lost the highest percentage of fat-free mass.

nodes.label: US Navy circumference body-fat method (Hodgdon & Beckett 1984) — ADOPTED
nodes.rationale: Predicts density via log10(circumferences), then Siri %BF=100*[(4.95/D)-4.50]. Accuracy vs hydrostatic weighing: men R=0.90 SEE 3.52%BF, women R=0.85 SEE 3.72%BF. Known bias (Potter 2022 vs DXA): underestimates men ~2.5%BF, overestimates women 1.3-2.3%BF; 'not suitable for applications requiring quantitative body composition assessment' — use only for tracking change over time. Three implementation traps: metric/imperial forms are not algebraically equivalent; abdomen site differs by sex (Abdomen II men, Abdomen I + hip women); Potter 2022 prints the female equation with the hip term omitted — a published typo, do not copy from there.
nodes.norm_label: us navy circumference body-fat method (hodgdon & beckett 1984) — adopted

nodes.label: Deurenberg BMI-based body-fat equation — REJECTED
nodes.rationale: %BF=1.20*BMI+0.23*age-10.8*sex-5.4, R2=0.79, SEE 4.1%BF (Deurenberg 1991). Lost because SEE 4.1 is worse than the Navy method's 3.52/3.72, and BMI cannot separate muscle from fat — fatal for an app whose purpose is tracking FFM change under resistance training.

nodes.label: Jackson-Pollock skinfold body-fat method — REJECTED
nodes.rationale: Comparable accuracy to the Navy method but lost on the stated constraint: needs calipers and a trained technician, which the app cannot supply.

nodes.label: Fractional weekly set-counting rule (direct set=1.0, indirect set=0.5) — ADOPTED
nodes.rationale: Supplied by Pelland 2025 (67 studies, 2,058 participants): posterior probability the volume slope exceeds zero is 100% for both hypertrophy and strength. Currier 2026 ACSM: hypertrophy enhanced by >=10 sets/wk, diminishing returns beyond ~18-20 weekly sets. The curve is monotonic increasing and decelerating — not a threshold and not an inverted U.
nodes.norm_label: fractional weekly set-counting rule (direct set=1.0, indirect set=0.5) — adopted

nodes.label: Baz-Valle 12-20 sets/week as a universal default — REJECTED (narrower population than needed)
nodes.rationale: Baz-Valle 2022 is sound (no difference moderate vs high for quadriceps p=0.19 or biceps p=0.59) but its population is young trained men 18-35 only, 7 studies. Currier 2023 BJSM (n>5,000, ~46% women) is the better generic anchor.
nodes.norm_label: baz-valle 12-20 sets/week as a universal default — rejected (narrower population than needed)

nodes.label: Split-selection engine keyed to available training days, 2-6 — ADOPTED
nodes.rationale: Frequency is a scheduling variable, not a growth variable (Schoenfeld/Grgic/Krieger 2019, verbatim: 'strong evidence that resistance training frequency does not significantly or meaningfully impact muscle hypertrophy when volume is equated'). 4-day Upper/Lower x2 is the engine default, matching Currier 2023's highest-ranked hypertrophy prescription (SMD 0.66).
nodes.norm_label: split-selection engine keyed to available training days, 2-6 — adopted

nodes.label: IOM (2005) sex-specific fluid baseline — ADOPTED
nodes.rationale: AI for total water: 3.7 L/d men, 2.7 L/d women; beverages supply 3.0 L / 2.2 L (~81% of total, food ~19%). Display the beverage figure, never the total AI, since an app cannot measure water in food.

nodes.label: '8x8' (eight glasses of water a day) rule — REJECTED
nodes.rationale: Valtin 2002 verbatim: 'No scientific studies were found in support of 8x8.' Also sex-invariant where the DRI is not, and wrongly excludes caffeinated beverages.
nodes.norm_label: '8x8' (eight glasses of water a day) rule — rejected

nodes.label: Rest-interval defaults stratified by load class (180-300s heavy compound / 120-180s moderate / 60-90s isolation) — ADOPTED, with an honest limit stated
nodes.rationale: de Salles 2009 (3-5 min at 50-90% 1RM), Grgic 2018 (>2 min in trained), Schoenfeld 2016 (3 min beat 1 min for 1RM squat/bench/quad thickness). Honest limit: the literature stratifies rest by LOAD AND GOAL, not by exercise type — the exercise-type mapping is an engineering heuristic (INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE for exercise-type stratification per se). ACSM 2026 found a null for rest interval on strength, but 'a null is not a reason to choose the short option.'
nodes.norm_label: rest-interval defaults stratified by load class (180-300s heavy compound / 120-180s moderate / 60-90s isolation) — adopted, with an honest limit stated

nodes.label: 30-60 s 'hypertrophy rest' default — REJECTED
nodes.rationale: de Salles 2009 itself recommended it, reasoning from acute growth-hormone response. Lost because the direct longitudinal test (Schoenfeld 2016) found 1 min WORSE than 3 min, substituting an acute endocrine surrogate for a measured morphological outcome.

nodes.label: Double progression with a %-of-load increment and an equipment-floor guard clause — ADOPTED
nodes.rationale: Delta_target = p*L (p=2.5% upper-body/isolation, p=5.0% lower-body compound); rounded down to nearest achievable equipment step; guard: if Delta_min/L>0.10, do not add load, extend the rep range instead. Citable anchor: ACSM 2009 verbatim 'it is recommended that 2-10% increase in load be applied'. The narrower 2.5%/5% split itself is INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — no study compares increment sizes head-to-head; it is a heuristic sitting inside the guideline range. The guard clause is the real engineering content: a 20 kg curl in a metric gym faces Delta_min=2.5kg=12.5% of working load, and dumbbells are the worst case (bilateral step is 2x the barbell step from an equivalent plate pair).
nodes.norm_label: double progression with a %-of-load increment and an equipment-floor guard clause — adopted

nodes.label: Velocity-based autoregulation as the progression trigger — REJECTED (on instrumentation, not evidence)
nodes.rationale: Zourdos 2016 shows velocity is the better construct — it is the variable RIR-based RPE was validated against (r=-0.88 experienced). It lost on instrumentation: a linear position transducer or validated accelerometer per set is required, against RIR's zero hardware.
nodes.norm_label: velocity-based autoregulation as the progression trigger — rejected (on instrumentation, not evidence)

nodes.label: Creatine dosed by body mass, not sex — ADOPTED
nodes.rationale: Engine rule: maintenance max(3 g, 0.1 g/kg), capped near 10 g/d; optional load 0.3 g/kg/d x 5-7 d. Kreider 2017: maintenance 3-5 g/day (larger athletes may need 5-10 g/day); safety up to 30 g/day for 5 years. Antonio 2021: loading is not required ('you do not have to load creatine'); neither source gives a sex-specific dose despite discussing sex — dose by body mass, and Antonio refutes testosterone, hair-loss, and kidney-damage objections at recommended doses.
nodes.norm_label: creatine dosed by body mass, not sex — adopted

nodes.label: Creatine ethyl ester and buffered creatine (Kre-Alkalyn) — REJECTED
nodes.rationale: Kreider 2017 Position #5 verbatim: 'creatine monohydrate is the most extensively studied and clinically effective form... in terms of muscle uptake'. These alternate forms lose on the exact outcome their marketing claims superiority on, and switching forms discards the entire safety database.
nodes.norm_label: creatine ethyl ester and buffered creatine (kre-alkalyn) — rejected
