nodes.label: Card c001: MPS elevated 24-48h; 20-40g protein across 3-5 meals
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Aragon & Schoenfeld (2013) is misordered (Schoenfeld is second author); paper supports rejecting the anabolic-window myth and gives 0.4-0.5 g/kg LBM per meal, but contains no 24-48h MPS statement.
nodes.norm_label: card c001: mps elevated 24-48h; 20-40g protein across 3-5 meals

nodes.label: Card c002: stretch>contraction; slow eccentrics produce more hypertrophy per joule
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Maeo 2021 is Med Sci Sports Exerc, not Eur J Sport Sci. Long-length half supported; tempo half contradicted by Schoenfeld/Ogborn/Krieger 2015 (hypertrophy similar 0.5-8s). 'Per joule' is not a reported quantity.
nodes.norm_label: card c002: stretch>contraction; slow eccentrics produce more hypertrophy per joule

nodes.label: Card c003: Epley 1RM formula w*(1+reps/30); 100x5->116kg; ~5% accurate
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Epley 1985 is a self-published, non-peer-reviewed poundage chart. Arithmetic itself is off: 100*(1+5/30)=116.7, not 116. The '~5% accurate for trained lifters' claim is unsupported (Reynolds 2006 reports SEE 1.85-14.05 kg).
nodes.norm_label: card c003: epley 1rm formula w*(1+reps/30); 100x5->116kg; ~5% accurate

nodes.label: Card c004: 1996 caffeine/creatine paper used 5mg/kg co-ingested; modern reviews find no interaction
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Trexler & Smith-Ryan (2015) journal mis-cited. The card inverts its own source: the 2015 review states caffeine 'may blunt the ergogenic effect of creatine'. The 1996 paper (Vandenberghe) used 6-day dosing, not single-dose.
nodes.norm_label: card c004: 1996 caffeine/creatine paper used 5mg/kg co-ingested; modern reviews find no interaction

nodes.label: Card c005: 10-20 sets/wk optimal volume; curve flattens at 22-25 sets
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Schoenfeld 2017 (verified) supports the graded dose-response (+0.023 ES/set, P=0.002) but the '10-20' band and '22-25 plateau' are not in the paper; the model is linear and detects no plateau at all.
nodes.norm_label: card c005: 10-20 sets/wk optimal volume; curve flattens at 22-25 sets

nodes.label: Card c006: 8h sleep raises T 10-15% vs 5h; GH in 4-5 pulses; one bad night costs 4-6% strength
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Leproult & Van Cauter 2011: the 8h condition was an at-home run-in, not the comparator; direction is inverted (restriction decreased daytime T). GH and strength claims are absent from this citation.
nodes.norm_label: card c006: 8h sleep raises t 10-15% vs 5h; gh in 4-5 pulses; one bad night costs 4-6% strength

nodes.label: Card c007 'Vyvanse and the heart': LDX raises HR 5-15bpm, SBP 3-7mmHg — MUST BE DELETED (Section 7, medical content)
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Coghill 2014 Table 2 at 70mg reports +4.1-5.4bpm/+1.3-2.6mmHg; the card's ranges are ~3x and non-overlapping.
nodes.norm_label: card c007 'vyvanse and the heart': ldx raises hr 5-15bpm, sbp 3-7mmhg — must be deleted (section 7, medical content)

nodes.label: Card c008: DOMS is not a proxy for training quality
nodes.rationale: WRONG (journal only, science sound) — Nosaka/Newton/Sacco 2002 is Scand J Med Sci Sports, not MSSE. The underlying claim is well supported (higher damage doses did not increase soreness, r<0.32).
nodes.norm_label: card c008: doms is not a proxy for training quality

nodes.label: Card c009: protein TEF 25-30%; net 600 of 800 kcal
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Westerterp verbatim gives 20-30% for protein; card narrows without warrant, and the arithmetic double-counts TEF by subtracting it from intake while also using an activity-factor TDEE.
nodes.norm_label: card c009: protein tef 25-30%; net 600 of 800 kcal

nodes.label: Card c010: deep squats produce less knee shear than partial squats
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Hartmann 2013 headline supported but mechanism wrong: compressive stress (not shear) peaks near 90 degrees; posterior/PCL shear is actually higher at parallel depth than quarter depth.
nodes.norm_label: card c010: deep squats produce less knee shear than partial squats

nodes.label: Card c011: tonnage is a useful stimulus proxy; ~6 million kg cumulative
nodes.rationale: WRONG (twice) — Mangine 2015 cuts against the card (lower-tonnage group gained more lean mass and strength); the app's own computed cumulative tonnage is ~0.6-0.8 million kg, an order of magnitude below the claimed 6 million.
nodes.norm_label: card c011: tonnage is a useful stimulus proxy; ~6 million kg cumulative

nodes.label: Card c012: Robusta 2.2-2.7% vs arabica 1.2-1.5% caffeine; condensed milk macros; stick ~120mg
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Belay 2008 is an Ethiopian-arabica-only analytical paper containing none of the cited numbers and no robusta data.
nodes.norm_label: card c012: robusta 2.2-2.7% vs arabica 1.2-1.5% caffeine; condensed milk macros; stick ~120mg

nodes.label: Card c013 'Hydration and Vyvanse': amphetamines reduce thirst; 3-4 L/day; dehydration causes headaches — MUST BE DELETED (Section 7, medical content)
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Boellner 2010 is a pediatric (ages 6-12) single-dose PK study in Clinical Therapeutics, not Pediatrics, and says nothing about thirst, dehydration or headache.
nodes.norm_label: card c013 'hydration and vyvanse': amphetamines reduce thirst; 3-4 l/day; dehydration causes headaches — must be deleted (section 7, medical content)

nodes.label: Card c014: push-up loads 64% BW; 41% at 30deg elevation; 74% at 30deg decline
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Suprak 2011 studied only traditional/knees-down push-ups; the 64/41/74 triple belongs to Ebben 2011, which used box heights (61.0 cm), not angles.
nodes.norm_label: card c014: push-up loads 64% bw; 41% at 30deg elevation; 74% at 30deg decline

nodes.label: Card c015: whey peaks 60-90min, casein 3-4h; leucine +220-280% vs +90-120%
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Boirie 1997: casein peaked at the same ~80min as whey; its distinguishing feature is duration, not delayed peak. No numeric plasma leucine percentages are reported; real Ra-ratio values are ~283%/~132%.
nodes.norm_label: card c015: whey peaks 60-90min, casein 3-4h; leucine +220-280% vs +90-120%

nodes.label: Card u001: stapedius ~1mm, smallest skeletal muscle
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Gray's Anatomy 42nd ed supports 'smallest skeletal muscle' but pooled mean length is 3.77-4.91mm, roughly 4-5x the card's figure.
nodes.norm_label: card u001: stapedius ~1mm, smallest skeletal muscle

nodes.label: Card u002: soleus 80-90% slow-twitch; orbicularis oculi ~100% fast; rarely shifts past 70:30
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Johnson 1973 metadata correct; soleus 80-90% COULD NOT VERIFY (secondary sources split ~70-87%); orbicularis oculi likely not among the 36 studied muscles and measured values are ~82-92% type II; the 70:30 training claim has no source.
nodes.norm_label: card u002: soleus 80-90% slow-twitch; orbicularis oculi ~100% fast; rarely shifts past 70:30

nodes.label: Card u003: Milo of Croton as the earliest reference to progressive overload
nodes.rationale: SUPPORTED — Quintilian's Institutio Oratoria I.9.5 verified; noted as a rhetorical chria (teaching example), not a training account.
nodes.norm_label: card u003: milo of croton as the earliest reference to progressive overload

nodes.label: Card u004: creatine isolated 1832 by Chevreul from meat broth; Harris 1992 showed oral loading works
nodes.rationale: SUPPORTED — Harris 1992 loading data verified; minor imprecision, Chevreul used an alkaline water extract of skeletal muscle, not 'meat broth'.
nodes.norm_label: card u004: creatine isolated 1832 by chevreul from meat broth; harris 1992 showed oral loading works

nodes.label: Card u005: 2x/wk gives ~3.1% more growth than 1x in trained lifters; 3x adds nothing
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Schoenfeld/Ogborn/Krieger 2016: the 3.1% figure (95% CI 1.6-4.6, P=0.003) is correctly transcribed, but the pooled cohorts were dominated by untrained subjects, not 'trained lifters', and the paper explicitly could not resolve 3x/week. See Section 2: Schoenfeld 2019 later showed this frequency effect is a volume artifact.
nodes.norm_label: card u005: 2x/wk gives ~3.1% more growth than 1x in trained lifters; 3x adds nothing

nodes.label: Card u006: trap bar gives 20-30% lower lumbar shear; 5-8% slower bar speed
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Camara 2016 measured EMG and force/power/velocity, not lumbar shear; the velocity claim is backwards (trap bar ~11% faster). The lumbar claim traces to Swinton 2011, which reported lower peak moments, not shear.
nodes.norm_label: card u006: trap bar gives 20-30% lower lumbar shear; 5-8% slower bar speed

nodes.label: Card u007: lifters are 5-10x stronger in horizontal push than pull
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Cools 2007 is an EMG scapular-activation study in Am J Sports Med (mis-cited journal), containing no push-vs-pull strength comparison; measured push:pull 1RM ratios cluster near 1:1.
nodes.norm_label: card u007: lifters are 5-10x stronger in horizontal push than pull

nodes.label: Card u008: untrained men gain 4-6kg lean yr1, 2-3 yr2, ~1 yr3
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Lambert & Flynn 2002 is a review of fatigue mechanisms in bodybuilding, containing no year-by-year gain figures; no peer-reviewed primary source was found for the table.
nodes.norm_label: card u008: untrained men gain 4-6kg lean yr1, 2-3 yr2, ~1 yr3

nodes.label: Card u009: 3mg/kg caffeine cuts RPE 5-7%, improves time-to-exhaustion 3-5%
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Grgic 2020 (card cites the DOI-suffix year 2019 in error) umbrella review reports no 3mg/kg dose-specific effect; RPE -5.6% is consistent but the endurance improvement was actually 12.3% (95% CI 9.1-15.4), not 3-5%.

nodes.rationale: WRONG — the anecdote is Athenaeus's (Deipnosophists 10.412-413, citing Poseidippus), not Galen's; Athenaeus separately attributes an ox-eating feat to Milo, not Theagenes.

nodes.rationale: WRONG (reverses its source) — Adams & Roughley 2006 states 'excessive mechanical loading disrupts a disc's structure' and lists loading history among the CAUSES of degeneration, not a protective factor.

nodes.label: Card u014: ONE hard set/muscle/week within 2 reps of failure maintains ~95% strength for 8-12 weeks
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Bickel/Cross/Bamman 2011: maintenance phase was 32 weeks, not 8-12; the leanest dose was 3 sets/wk, not one; effort was volitional fatigue, not 2 RIR; after 32 weeks of complete detraining strength fell only 7%.

nodes.label: Card u015: 10wk heavy squats improve 5km running economy 5% via stiffer Achilles and faster ground contact
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Storen 2008 duration was 8 weeks, not 10; the 5% economy figure is right but measured at 70% VO2max, not '5km economy'; the paper measured neither tendon stiffness nor ground contact time.

nodes.rationale: WRONG — Hamilton 2022 contains zero occurrences of 'mitochondrial density' and characterises the soleus at ~88% type I with no %MVC reported; the standing-break claim is contradicted by the paper's own cited source (standing did not reduce glucose vs sitting).

nodes.label: Card r002: Galen linked diet/training/recovery first; prescribed pork and beans; banned from Rome for ridiculing Hippocrates
nodes.rationale: WRONG — wrong Galen title cited; the 'banned from Rome' claim is backwards (Galen venerated Hippocrates); 'pork and beans' is contradicted by Losch 2014's gladiator-diet study (wheat, barley, legumes).
nodes.norm_label: card r002: galen linked diet/training/recovery first; prescribed pork and beans; banned from rome for ridiculing hippocrates

nodes.label: Card r003: MSTN knockout child lifted 3kg dumbbells at age 4
nodes.rationale: SUPPORTED — Schuelke 2004 verified; correction: the child was 4.5 years old, not 4.
nodes.norm_label: card r003: mstn knockout child lifted 3kg dumbbells at age 4

nodes.label: Card r004: women's pull-up capacity equals men's once strength-to-mass is controlled
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Vanderburgh & Flanagan 2000 is an unrelated male-only backpack-run study with no pull-ups or women; Miller 1993 shows women only ~52% as strong as men in the upper body, with equality only in force per unit muscle cross-sectional area.
nodes.norm_label: card r004: women's pull-up capacity equals men's once strength-to-mass is controlled

nodes.label: Card r005: resistance training depresses immunity 2-24h; gym-goers get ~40% fewer URTIs
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Walsh 2011 makes no resistance-training immunosuppression claim and questions the 'open window' itself; the 40% figure actually traces to Nieman 2011 (43% fewer URTI days, for AEROBIC exercise, self-reported).
nodes.norm_label: card r005: resistance training depresses immunity 2-24h; gym-goers get ~40% fewer urtis

nodes.label: Card r006: Topham lifted ~800kg; mid-thigh pull 270kg
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — the ~800kg (1,836 lb / 833 kg) hogshead feat is independently documented via a contemporary etching; the 270kg mid-thigh-pull figure is COULD NOT VERIFY.
nodes.norm_label: card r006: topham lifted ~800kg; mid-thigh pull 270kg

nodes.label: Card r007: exercise rhinitis from parasympathetic rebound after sympathetic arousal
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Silvers 1991 is in Annals of Allergy, not J Allergy Clin Immunol, and shows cold-induced rhinorrhoea is cholinergic, not parasympathetic rebound; exercise itself normally produces sympathetic nasal decongestion.
nodes.norm_label: card r007: exercise rhinitis from parasympathetic rebound after sympathetic arousal

nodes.label: Card r008: one night total sleep deprivation cuts 1RM bench 8-12%; 4h x3 nights cuts 5-8%
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Reilly & Piercy 1994 used 3-hour sleep for 3 nights with no total-deprivation arm, so the card's headline has no basis in the cited paper; the specific percentages are COULD NOT VERIFY.
nodes.norm_label: card r008: one night total sleep deprivation cuts 1rm bench 8-12%; 4h x3 nights cuts 5-8%

nodes.label: Card r009: 85-90% of early strength gain is neural; visible growth starts weeks 6-10
nodes.rationale: UNSUPPORTED — Sale 1988's treatment is qualitative with no locatable 85-90% figure; Bontemps 2022 measured vastus lateralis ACSA growth of +2.9% at 2 weeks, contradicting the 'weeks 6-10' onset claim.
nodes.norm_label: card r009: 85-90% of early strength gain is neural; visible growth starts weeks 6-10

nodes.label: Card r010: blinded milk-vs-soy trials found identical 'mucus feeling'
nodes.rationale: WRONG (cites one paper, describes another) — the card cites Pinnock 1990 (no soy arm, no blinding); the design it actually describes is Pinnock & Arney 1993, where 3 of 14 indicators rose equally in both arms.
nodes.norm_label: card r010: blinded milk-vs-soy trials found identical 'mucus feeling'

nodes.label: Card r011: ice baths within 24h cut hypertrophy 25-30%
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Roberts 2015: cold-water immersion was applied within 5 minutes, not 24 hours; the real effect was ~67% less lean-mass gain than active recovery, and type II fibre CSA did not grow at all with CWI.
nodes.norm_label: card r011: ice baths within 24h cut hypertrophy 25-30%

nodes.label: Card r012: grip strength at 40 predicts mortality better than SBP or BMI; -5kg -> +16% risk over the following decade
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Leong 2015 (PURE study): HR 1.16 per 5kg and the SBP comparison are verbatim supported, but median follow-up was 4.0 years, not a decade; the cohort was aged 35-70 at enrolment, so 'at age 40' misdescribes it; BMI was an adjustment covariate, not a comparator.
nodes.norm_label: card r012: grip strength at 40 predicts mortality better than sbp or bmi; -5kg -> +16% risk over the following decade

nodes.label: C1: Unvalidated Import Bricks the App Permanently
nodes.rationale: Import merges untrusted JSON into state with only a typeof-object check; an out-of-range week/day or wrong-typed field throws inside usePlanStore's derived useMemo above every ErrorBoundary, and the hostile state is already persisted, so the crash reproduces on every reload with no in-app recovery. Fix: gate both import and localStorage rehydration through one schema validator, reject rather than coerce, and mount an error boundary above the store hook.
nodes.norm_label: c1: unvalidated import bricks the app permanently

nodes.label: H1: Prescription Medication and Health Profile Shipped as Public Static Assets
nodes.rationale: data.js and console-content.js hardcode a named drug and exact dose (Vyvanse 40 mg), a body-composition profile, and a daily routine as build-time constants that DEPLOY.md instructs uploading; on a URL carrying the user's surname this is GDPR Art. 9 special-category health data that becomes permanently public via git history once committed. Fix: keep PLAN a neutral template and load medication/profile data only from validated localStorage entered at setup.
nodes.norm_label: h1: prescription medication and health profile shipped as public static assets

nodes.label: H2: One-Click Unconfirmed Permanent Data Wipe
nodes.rationale: The persistent footer button clears fti.console.v2 and reloads with no confirm(), undo, or export prompt, unlike the sibling reset() which does gate on confirm(); combined with the missing frame-ancestors CSP directive, a clickjacking overlay needs only one click to destroy the user's data, and the wipe itself is incomplete since it leaves two other storage keys orphaned. Fix: delete the control and require typed confirmation plus an automatic export before any destructive action.
nodes.norm_label: h2: one-click unconfirmed permanent data wipe

nodes.label: H3: Silent localStorage Quota Failure Causes Silent Permanent Data Loss
nodes.rationale: saveV2 (and equivalents in core.jsx and console-video.jsx) wrap localStorage.setItem in an empty catch, so QuotaExceededError is discarded while React state and the UI already show the write as successful; the shared GitHub Pages origin makes exhaustion arrive earlier than the app's own growth predicts. Fix: catch QuotaExceededError explicitly, surface a blocking banner, and move persistence to IndexedDB.
nodes.norm_label: h3: silent localstorage quota failure causes silent permanent data loss

nodes.label: H4: Date Helpers Mix UTC and Local Time
nodes.rationale: todayISO round-trips a civil date through toISOString (UTC) while isoDaysBetween/isoOffset parse local time, so the program day shifts by one across a DST transition and by timezone offset near midnight; programPosition derives training day/week from this arithmetic, permanently desynchronising the program for any non-UTC user. Measured empirically under Node across four timezones. Fix: use date-fns or Temporal.PlainDate for civil-date arithmetic and persist the user's IANA timezone.
nodes.norm_label: h4: date helpers mix utc and local time

nodes.label: M1: No Content-Security-Policy, and the Architecture Forbids a Strict One
nodes.rationale: GitHub Pages sends no CSP header, and runtime Babel-in-browser JSX compilation requires 'unsafe-eval' while the inline script requires 'unsafe-inline', so any CSP under the current architecture provides essentially no script-injection protection. The Vite rewrite removes the structural cause by compiling JSX at build time, enabling a strict meta-tag CSP with frame-ancestors 'none'.
nodes.norm_label: m1: no content-security-policy, and the architecture forbids a strict one

nodes.label: M2: Third-Party Video Iframe With No Sandbox on Hardcoded Community Hosts
nodes.rationale: The Invidious iframe has no sandbox attribute, so a cross-origin instance could top-navigate the app via sticky user activation from video playback if any of six hardcoded hobbyist domains is ever re-registered by a new owner; the URL construction itself is safe (regex-gated videoId, encodeURIComponent). Fix: add sandbox without allow-top-navigation/allow-popups and pin hosts in frame-src.
nodes.norm_label: m2: third-party video iframe with no sandbox on hardcoded community hosts

nodes.label: M3: Service Worker Caches Cross-Origin Scripts Unverified and Fakes Offline Readiness
nodes.rationale: Install swallows failed shell-fetch errors so skipWaiting() activates an incomplete cache and the app advertises offline support it lacks; cached unpkg responses carry no integrity check, and a stale 'piped.' string-match exclusion was never updated after the app moved to Invidious. Fix: adopt vite-plugin-pwa/Workbox with content-hashed, all-or-nothing precaching and origin-based routing.
nodes.norm_label: m3: service worker caches cross-origin scripts unverified and fakes offline readiness

nodes.label: M4: Shared vkotzamanis.github.io Origin Exposes localStorage to Every Other Project
nodes.rationale: localStorage is scoped to origin, not path, so any other project hosted on the same GitHub Pages account origin can read the complete training log via fti.console.v2; this also shares the quota budget that feeds H3. Fix: host the rewrite on a dedicated origin if data stays in web storage — IndexedDB is equally origin-scoped and does not solve this.
nodes.norm_label: m4: shared vkotzamanis.github.io origin exposes localstorage to every other project

nodes.label: M5: No Schema Version or Migration; Three Uncoordinated Storage Keys
nodes.rationale: The 'v2' suffix in fti.console.v2 is documentation, not an enforced version field, so a key whose type changed is exactly what C1 exploits; three uncoordinated keys mean the wipe button and export/import each touch only one, leaving stale orphans. Fix: an explicit schemaVersion field, an ordered migration chain, and consolidation to one key.
nodes.norm_label: m5: no schema version or migration; three uncoordinated storage keys

nodes.label: M6: Primary Set-Log Path Accepts Negative, Unbounded, and Infinite Weight/Reps
nodes.rationale: submit() checks only !isNaN, which is false for Infinity, unlike the correctly range-gated body-weight and push-up inputs elsewhere in the same codebase; an imported value like 1e999 parses to Infinity, propagates into makeCoachLine/suggestedLoad and an SVG path that silently stops rendering, and round-trips through JSON.stringify as null on export. Fix: validate with Number.isFinite against a bounded plausible range, matching the import schema.
nodes.norm_label: m6: primary set-log path accepts negative, unbounded, and infinite weight/reps

nodes.label: M7: waterTarget Drives an Unbounded Render Loop
nodes.rationale: Array.from({length: s.waterTarget}) has no UI setter but is a persisted, importable field; an imported value like 100000000 makes React attempt to construct one hundred million elements on the default view, freezing the tab in a way no ErrorBoundary can catch since it is a hang, not a throw. Fix: covered by schema bounds, plus defence-in-depth clamping at the render site.
nodes.norm_label: m7: watertarget drives an unbounded render loop

nodes.label: M8: Unauthenticated Message Listeners, Wildcard postMessage, and Dev Tooling in Production
nodes.rationale: tweaks-panel.jsx's message listeners never check e.origin/e.source and its postMessage calls unconditionally target '*'; combined with the missing frame-ancestors directive, any framing page receives every wildcard broadcast, and the 568-line dev tool ships to production with a second, dead, unread s.tweaks state branch. Fix: gate the panel behind import.meta.env.DEV, require origin allowlisting on every listener, and delete the unused branch.
nodes.norm_label: m8: unauthenticated message listeners, wildcard postmessage, and dev tooling in production

nodes.label: L1: Google Fonts Stylesheet — No SRI, Client IP Disclosure, Offline Breakage
nodes.rationale: The per-user-agent-generated Google Fonts CSS cannot carry a stable SRI hash and discloses IP/User-Agent to Google on an app whose stated premise is on-device-only data; it is also absent from the service worker's precache list, so installed offline use falls back to system fonts. Fix: self-host via @fontsource, fingerprinted and bundled at build time.
nodes.norm_label: l1: google fonts stylesheet — no sri, client ip disclosure, offline breakage

nodes.label: L2: React Development Builds Served in Production
nodes.rationale: index.html loads react.development.js/react-dom.development.js, which are several times larger and run per-render invariant checks, though the SRI hashes are correct and pinned — this is the wrong artifact, not an unverified one. Vite's production build resolves it automatically.
nodes.norm_label: l2: react development builds served in production

nodes.label: L3: No Referrer-Policy
nodes.rationale: index.html sets no document-wide referrer meta tag, leaving the unstated browser default, though the video iframe and its links already set referrerPolicy/rel individually and correctly. Fix: add an explicit no-referrer meta tag.

nodes.label: L4: Service Worker SKIP_WAITING Handler Validates Nothing
nodes.rationale: self.skipWaiting() fires on any message of type SKIP_WAITING without checking event.origin/event.source; exposure is small because service worker clients are same-origin by definition. Fix: check event.source is a controlled client and let vite-plugin-pwa own the update prompt.
nodes.norm_label: l4: service worker skip_waiting handler validates nothing

nodes.label: L5: DEPLOY.md Is Inverted Against the Current Tree
nodes.rationale: DEPLOY.md tells the deployer to upload the stale console.html as the app and withhold the actual live entry point index.html, and also instructs uploading data.js — the H1 disclosure path. Fix: delete console.html and let a Vite build's dist/ output replace the hand-maintained file list.
nodes.norm_label: l5: deploy.md is inverted against the current tree

nodes.label: L6: Invalid Set Submission Fails Silently
nodes.rationale: submit() and the range-gated inputs elsewhere return early on invalid input with no message, focus change, or styling, leaving the user unaware their action did nothing. Fix: surface a validation message on rejection.
nodes.norm_label: l6: invalid set submission fails silently

nodes.label: I1: No XSS Sink Exists Anywhere in the Codebase (Verified Absent)
nodes.rationale: An exhaustive grep for dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval, new Function, srcdoc, and javascript: across all application files returns zero hits; every user-controlled string reaches the DOM only via JSX children, which React escapes.
nodes.norm_label: i1: no xss sink exists anywhere in the codebase (verified absent)

nodes.label: I2: The Import Merge Is Not Prototype-Pollutable (Verified Absent)
nodes.rationale: Object spread in the import merge uses CreateDataProperty (define semantics), not Set, so a __proto__ key survives only as an inert own property; verified empirically that ({}).polluted stays undefined after importing a __proto__ payload. This is a property of the spread operator, not a deliberate guard — Object.assign in the same position would be exploitable. C1 remains a state-shape injection, not a pollution vector.
nodes.norm_label: i2: the import merge is not prototype-pollutable (verified absent)

nodes.label: I3: No Tracking, Analytics, or Outbound Telemetry (Verified Absent)
nodes.rationale: No analytics, beacons, error reporting, or WebSocket exist; the only fetch call in the codebase is the service worker's own cache-refresh fetch, and the codebase's 'telemetry' is a local toast-message generator, not network traffic.
nodes.norm_label: i3: no tracking, analytics, or outbound telemetry (verified absent)

nodes.label: I4: No Secrets, Keys, or Credentials (Verified Absent)
nodes.rationale: A scan for API keys, tokens, passwords, bearer credentials, cloud provider key prefixes, and PEM blocks across all source files returns nothing; the sensitive data present is personal health data (H1), not credential material.
nodes.norm_label: i4: no secrets, keys, or credentials (verified absent)

nodes.label: Absent: URL Injection in the Video Modal
nodes.rationale: videoId is gated by an 11-character regex, hosts come from a compile-time array, and search terms pass through encodeURIComponent, so the iframe's missing sandbox is a privilege problem rather than an injection one.
nodes.norm_label: absent: url injection in the video modal

nodes.label: Absent: Insecure Transport
nodes.rationale: No http:// URLs exist in the codebase; GitHub Pages serves HTTPS with HSTS.
